prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In a top-down egocentric view looking down at a stone patio, the depth map grades the camera wearer's grey-shirted torso as the nearest surface (0.1–0.3 m, brightest white) and the extended forearms and hands manipulating a small green object within arm's reach at roughly 0.4–0.5 m in front of and below the camera. Further below on the ground (~1.2–1.8 m away) sit a cylindrical bucket to the upper-left, branches and a round planter bucket to the upper-right (spaced ~0.6–0.8 m apart), a curved retaining edge along the left, and in frame 5 a second person's lower legs and a rectangular block or step entering at the top edge (~1.5–1.8 m in front of the wearer). Across frames 1 to 4, the wearer's hands move slightly closer together until the fingers touch and partially occlude the held object, while in frame 5 the camera pitches slightly upward and the hands drop slightly lower in the frame as the second person's legs appear ahead facing roughly toward the wearer's left/front. The depth map clearly reveals the 3D elevation of the cylindrical containers, raised stone border, and sticks on the patio floor that are washed out by severe lens glare and sunlight in the RGB image. However, the map is unreliable on the thin held object and the gaps between the fingers where depth bleeds smoothly into the background, and it flattens fine ground textures in the darkest shadow regions.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's lower torso, arms, and hands in the lower half of the frame (0.1–0.5 m from the camera, with the held object within direct grasp) and detects the second person's lower legs entering at the top-center of frame 5 (~1.5–1.8 m ahead, standing near the patio containers with their upper body cropped out of view above the frame). Across frames 1 to 4, the wearer's left and right arms extend forward from the bottom corners toward the center as the hands converge and overlap in frame 4, then separate slightly in frame 5 as the distant person's legs appear in front of the wearer. Compared to the glare-heavy RGB strip, segmentation sharply delineates the outer silhouette of the wearer's body and immediately highlights the presence and position of the second person's legs at the top edge of frame 5. However, the map is highly unreliable for scene layout and object identity because it completely misses all background objects—including the held green piece, the buckets, sticks, and patio walls—leaving them as unlabelled black void. It also suffers from severe over-segmentation on the camera wearer in frames 2, 3, and 4, splitting the wearer's left arm, right arm, and torso into two or three separate 'person' instances with overlapping labels.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints of the camera wearer's hands (magenta) held at roughly 0.4–0.5 m in front of and below the head, along with an upper-body/arm skeleton (yellow) in frame 1 spanning from the shoulders (~0.2 m) down the arms to the wrists. The left and right hand skeletons are positioned left and right of center within a few centimetres of each other, pinching the small held object within immediate reach while the rest of the wearer's lower body and the background scene remain unrepresented. Across the five frames, the two magenta hand skeletons angled inward toward each other draw closer from ~0.1 m apart in frames 1–3 to overlapping contact in frame 4, before separating slightly and shifting downward in frame 5 as the camera tilts up. This map makes the fine finger articulations and pinch posture of the right hand much easier to read in frames 1–4 where strong sun flare washes out the right hand in the RGB image. Nonetheless, it is unreliable for broader spatial awareness because the yellow body keypoints hallucinate facial nodes on the wearer's chest in frame 1, vanish entirely in frames 2–5, and fail to detect the second person's legs visible at the top of frame 5.
